svg.aria-label: Ten small panels, one per skill in taught order, each with a pale band of raw training loss, a teal smoothed training-loss line and an amber held-out-loss line on a log scale against updates within the skill.
svg.text: Each skill during its own teach: training loss and held-out loss
raw training loss, min to max
held-out loss on 8 monitored panel rows, every 25 updates
9,850 updates · held-out loss at the end 9.1e-05 nats
3,557 updates · held-out loss at the end 0.16 nats
3,600 updates · held-out loss at the end 0.37 nats
3,568 updates · held-out loss at the end 0.059 nats
21,309 updates · held-out loss at the end 0.00061 nats
3,911 updates · held-out loss at the end 0.031 nats
7,871 updates · held-out loss at the end 0.034 nats
measured where the teach resumed and at its end
2,835 updates · held-out loss at the end 0.045 nats
measured at the start and the end of this teach
3,025 updates · held-out loss at the end 0.015 nats
3,756 updates · held-out loss at the end 0.093 nats
All ten panels share one loss axis (1e-5 to 10 nats, log scale). The held-out curve is the mean per-token loss on eight fixed
panel rows that are never trained on, measured every 25 updates; it is a monitor, not the 225-row evaluation. During the PCFG
and Tessel teaches the every-25-update monitor watched the previously taught skills and the English control rather than the
skill being taught; that skill was measured on the same eight rows at the gate instead, once before its first update and once
after its last, and those two points are drawn with a dashed segment between them. The PCFG point sits 792 updates in because
that teach was resumed there; the Tessel point sits at the start of its teach. Source:
